sections.heading: Section 2: Sliding Ladders and Pythagorean Triangles

questions.q: A $13\text{-ft}$ ladder leans against a vertical wall. If the bottom slides away from the wall at $2\text{ ft/s}$, how fast is the top sliding down when the bottom is $5\text{ ft}$ from the wall?
Two cars start from the same point. Car A travels north at $40\text{ mph}$ and Car B travels east at $30\text{ mph}$. How fast is the distance between them increasing after 2 hours?
questions.answer: After 2 h: $y = 80\text{ miles}, x = 60\text{ miles}, z = \sqrt{60^2 + 80^2} = 100\text{ miles}$. $2z\frac{dz}{dt} = 2x\frac{dx}{dt} + 2y\frac{dy}{dt} \Rightarrow 100\frac{dz}{dt} = 60(30) + 80(40) = 1800 + 3200 = 5000 \Rightarrow \frac{dz}{dt} = 50\text{ mph}$.

questions.q: In the 13-ft ladder problem ($x = 5, y = 12, dx/dt = 2$), at what rate is the area of the triangle formed by the ladder changing?
Water flows into an inverted conical tank (radius $4\text{ m}$, height $12\text{ m}$) at $2\text{ m}^3\text{/min}$. How fast is the water level rising when the depth is $6\text{ m}$?
questions.answer: By similar triangles, $r/h = 4/12 = 1/3 \Rightarrow r = h/3$. $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi(h/3)^2 h = \frac{\pi}{27}h^3$. $\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{\pi}{9}h^2 \frac{dh}{dt}$. At $h = 6$: $2 = \frac{\pi}{9}(36)\frac{dh}{dt} = 4\pi \frac{dh}{dt} \Rightarrow \frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{2}{4\pi} = \frac{1}{2\pi}\text{ m/min}$.

questions.q: A cylindrical tank of radius $3\text{ m}$ is being filled at $18\pi\text{ m}^3\text{/min}$. How fast is the water height increasing?
A trough with triangular cross-section (base $2\text{ m}$, depth $2\text{ m}$, length $6\text{ m}$) leaks water at $0.5\text{ m}^3\text{/min}$. What is $dh/dt$ when $h = 1\text{ m}$?
questions.answer: Cross section base $b = h$. $V = \frac{1}{2}b h \times 6 = 3h^2$. $\frac{dV}{dt} = 6h \frac{dh}{dt}$. $-0.5 = 6(1)\frac{dh}{dt} \Rightarrow \frac{dh}{dt} = -\frac{0.5}{6} = -\frac{1}{12}\text{ m/min}$.

sections.heading: Section 4: Shadows and Angles of Elevation

questions.q: A 6-ft tall person walks away from a 15-ft streetlight at $4\text{ ft/s}$. At what rate is the length of the person's shadow increasing?
In the same streetlight scenario, at what rate is the tip of the shadow moving?
questions.answer: Tip position is $x + s = x + \frac{2}{3}x = \frac{5}{3}x$. Rate of tip $= \frac{5}{3}\frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{5}{3}(4) = \frac{20}{3}\text{ ft/s}$.
